subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Origami Engineering: Folding for Function
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Origami Engineering: Folding for Function.

hook.text: Paper folding isn't just art. Engineers now use it to design real machines.

buildup.text: Fold patterns let flat sheets transform into 3-D structures in one motion.

discovery.text: One fold pattern can collapse a satellite solar panel for launch and deploy in orbit.

twist.text: The Miura fold lets a large map collapse and open with a single pull.

climax.text: Heart stents, airbags, and space antennas all borrow from origami math.

punchline.text: The art of folding paper now folds metal in space.

quiz.question: Why is origami engineering useful for space applications?
options: Paper is lighter than metal in zero gravity
Fold patterns let large structures collapse small for launch and deploy in orbit
Origami shapes are stronger than traditional engineering structures
